support-bot: ALERT: High p99 latency observed for hosted API in eu-west-1 affecting customer sprockets-inc — ticket #CI-1329. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~450ms, p99 ~1.8s (baseline p99 ~220ms). Spike started 2026-03-14T11:02:13Z. Links: https://grafana/reports/CI-1329 and trace sample id=trc-9b3f.

ana: Copying in eng-sre. Can someone grab a trace id and a sample request/response? Any recent deploys or infra changes in eu-west?

mike: I've pulled a few traces from the trace id — here's one curl reproducer from an internal edge node (note the long TLS connect):

```
curl -vv -o /dev/null -s -w "time_connect=%{time_connect} time_starttransfer=%{time_starttransfer}\n" https://api.eu-west.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
# output: time_connect=0.912 time_starttransfer=1.82
```

mike: So TLS handshake ~900ms, server processing ~900ms (combined ~1.8s). Tested from two different edge nodes in eu-west-1a and eu-west-1b, both show high connect times.

jorge: I ran traceroute from the edge node to the upstream ingress LB (priv net):

```
traceroute -n 10.0.12.57
 1 10.0.1.1 0.2 ms 0.2 ms 0.2 ms
 2 10.0.2.5 0.7 ms 0.8 ms 0.7 ms
 3 184.72.12.1 85.3 ms 86.1 ms 85.8 ms
 4 93.184.216.1 86.0 ms 86.2 ms 86.1 ms
 5 10.10.10.1 87.1 ms 87.0 ms 86.9 ms
```

jorge: That third hop jumps to a public transit ASN with ~85ms added latency — looks like traffic leaving our VPC and traversing a carrier. That would explain high TLS times.

ashley: We had a DNS failover event at 10:56 UTC — Route53 healthcheck flipped to secondary nameserver after 50s of failed healthchecks (shared in ops incident). Secondary DNS is via partner provider which has anycast points in different PoPs; maybe some of their PoPs route through a transit adding extra hops.

samir: Also saw a brief spike in upstream TLS handshake errors in the edge logs around the same time: `tls: handshake timeout` rate increased x4. Could be packet loss or asymmetric routing during DNS switch.

ana: Any recent envoy/edge config changes? Could SNI routing mismatch cause cross-az egress?

mike: No envoy rollouts in eu-west last 24h. There was a control-plane push to adjust `connect_timeout` on cluster upstreams a few hours earlier but that should only affect client timeouts, not route selection.

ashley: Quick mitigation idea: force edge egress to prefer internal transit path (apply static next-hop via NAT GW in same AZ) for sprockets’ VIP for 30m while we validate partner DNS reachability. Also lower DNS TTL for API domain (currently 300s) — but note TTL changes take effect after propagation.

jorge: Steps I suggest for investigation (ordered):
1) `tcpdump` on the edge node during repro to capture SYN/SYN-ACK RTTs 
2) dig +short from client to see which A records are returned and compare to expected Anycast IP sets
3) BGP path lookup for the partner ASN to check for origin prepends or blackholed prefixes
4) Check iptables/NAT table on edge node for any route overrides

mike: I already did a quick `dig` from an affected node — returns partner anycast address set (a.b.c.d).

```
$ dig +short api.eu-west.redwood.example
a.b.c.d
```

mike: I then `curl --resolve api.eu-west.redwood.example:a.b.c.d:443` to force that IP and saw the same TLS connect times, so DNS is pointing at partner infrastructure.

samir: I captured a 60s tcpdump focused on TLS SYNs — SYN->SYN/ACK RTTs are in the 850-950ms range, not just server processing. Packets show no retransmits but there is a long RTT to the partner anycast path.

ana: Okay, conclusion so far: partner DNS failover routed traffic via partner PoP -> transit provider -> our ingress, adding ~80ms extra hop and TLS handshake slows to ~900ms. That explains p99 spike. Next, mitigation plan:

- Immediate (temporary): add a temporary DNS override for sprockets-inc using our internal DNS resolver to return our primary Anycast IP (bypass partner), TTL 60s. Also apply an egress route override on edge nodes for the partner IP to prefer internal NAT GW for 1h.
- Short-term (hours): ask partner to investigate their PoP routing, provide BGP path and PoP mapping; open ticket with partner + cloud carrier.
- Medium (day): add better healthcheck and traffic steering rules to avoid partner PoPs with high RTT; add automated rollback to last-known-good DNS on failures.
- Longer-term: add passive latency monitoring to DNS failover so we only flip when path performance within threshold.

ashley: I can push the temporary DNS override in our internal resolver. I'll also update the runbook and set TTL 60s.

mike: I can apply the ip route add on affected edge nodes for the partner IP to prefer nat-gw. Rolling this to 25% of nodes first.

jorge: I'll open a ticket with the partner and attach traceroute/tcpdump + BGP path.

samir: After the route override + DNS override, I reran the same curl from the edge node: `time_connect=0.096 time_starttransfer=0.43`. p99 dropped to ~420ms in our dashboard (preliminary).

ana: Great. Let's treat this as mitigated but not resolved. Actions:
- ashley: apply DNS override + note in incident log (ETA 10m)
- mike: route override canary -> confirm latency improvement (ETA 20m)
- jorge: partner ticket (ETA 30m)
- samir: collect tcpdumps + metrics for the postmortem
- ana (me): schedule 1hr postmortem after stabilization and assign to eng-networking + eng-sre

ashley: DNS override applied at 11:28 UTC, TTL=60. Added comment in ops channel.

mike: Route override canary applied to 25% nodes at 11:35 UTC. Latency on canary nodes matches baseline. Rolling to remaining nodes now.

samir: Can confirm p99 improved to ~410-460ms across eu-west within ~5 minutes of full rollout. No increase in error rate.

jorge: Partner ticket created: PT-9473, attached traceroutes and tcpdump. Partner replies say they're seeing a misconfig at one PoP and will reroute within 4h.

ana: Thanks all. We'll leave DNS override + route override in place until partner confirms fix. Create a short postmortem with timeline + root cause + follow-ups (improve DNS failover logic, routing runbook). I'll own the postmortem and assign follow-ups to eng-networking.

mike: Quick note for follow-ups: consider enabling TLS session resumption on the edge egress for partner connections to reduce handshake cost for long-lived clients.

ashley: Added follow-up tasks in JIRA: RD-541 (postmortem), RD-542 (DNS failover improvements), RD-543 (routing automation).

ana: Closing thread for active work — will reopen if customer reports persistent issues. Thanks. :thumbsup:
